articleTitle: The application of IEC 61131-3 to industrial control: improve your bottom line through high value industrial control systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: Modern programming methods provide tools to improve the intrinsic quality of software, i.e. its correctness in the sense of reliability, robustness, integrity, persistence, and safety. The international standard IEC 1131-3 provides such a tool, dealing with the programming, installation and maintenance phases of software development projects in industrial control. Basically, IEC 1131-3 consists of two parts, i.e. common elements and programming languages. The structuring tools within IEC 1131-3 are focused on the common elements, although clearly links to the programming languages are needed. The article shows that by using IEC 1131-3 in a consistent way, one can generate software code that is better understandable, reusable, verifiable and maintainable.

articleTitle: An industrial case study covering the use of IEC 1131-3 in connection with the engineering and operation requirements of the water industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: Bechtel have utilised or drawn upon many areas of the IEC 1131-3 standard during the design of their library of standard software modules (SSMs) starting with function block diagrams and sequential function blocks through to structured text and ladder diagram. The resulting library of SSMs that have been developed, sit together so successfully in a truly modular form that it is possible to replace an updated SSM within a configured and operational system without affecting any other section of the system. The software engineering techniques promoted in IEC 1131-3 have enabled Bechtel to implement the SSM approach across new projects and will now help to get away from the past where bespoke code was developed time and time again resulting in a different approach to the same problem of control, site by site. Bechtel's engineers and their contractors are now implementing this philosophy on a large number of key contracts with several water utilities to assess the success of the project.

articleTitle: The impact of IEC (6)1131-3 on the teaching of control engineering
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: Graduates need to possess a balance of practical skills and theoretical knowledge. Within control engineering students must learn the basic principles of feedback system stability but also how to design, install and tune a practical control loop. The correct balance between principles, theory and technology is sometimes difficult to achieve. Education which is centred on particular equipment cannot give the breadth of exposure required. Further, when using a certain manufacturer's hardware or software, there is a danger that the exercise becomes simply training rather than broader based education. The paper looks at the teaching of traditional control engineering in further and higher education and examines the impact that IEC (6)1131-3 can have. An approach in which IEC (6)1131-3 compliant programming software is used with realistic simulations of a plant is described. This approach has been found to have many benefits for teaching and also for practising instrumentation and control engineers.

articleTitle: The importance of 61131 to UK business
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: The standard IEC 61131 is a complete framework for those in both the manufacturing and process industries involved in programmable controllers. Part 3 (61131-3) is the section concerning programming languages. It is my task to put the topic in the overall context of improving the competitiveness of British Industry against the ever increasing global competition, a daunting task for a humble engineer! In order to assess its importance in this respect, I put the standard in the wider context of improving our overall performance in the manufacturing and process sectors.

articleTitle: Application of IEC 61131 on BNFL Sellafield site
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: Explains how the use of IEC 61131 has been beneficial to the Sellafield Drypac Plant (SDP) project and what advantages BNFL have gained in the wider intermediate level waste standardisation strategy. The article covers control requirements and selection criteria; control system architecture; and typical device hardware/software implementation.

articleTitle: CJ international welcomes you to the soft logic open world
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: CJ International was founded in 1990 by a team of software engineers specialized in the development of soft logic tools that bridge the gap between microcomputer systems and PLCs. The software products offered by CJ International are based on industry standards. They bring modern PLC programming techniques to industrial microcomputers. CJ International is committed to providing innovative solutions that lead the way to the next generation of open PLCs according to IEC 61131 standards and mainly the chapter 3. The author charts the historical development of the ISaGRAF soft logic product with the development of IEC 61131-3 standard.

articleTitle: Lessons from a large systems protect
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: A multinational control systems company was supplying a system to manage a large pipeline distribution network overseas. The project included the supply of the communications infrastructure and SCADA system required for the real-time control of the pipeline network. The pipeline network included pump stations, valve sites, treatment plants, tank farms etc. The paper gives a retrospective view of the effectiveness with which IEC 61131-3 has been put to use by systems integrators and end users using equipment supplied by Arcom. The case study used is fictional in order that several issues may be discussed within the context of a single project, but is a composite of experiences gained in real systems over 3 years.

articleTitle: The application of IEC 61131-3 to industrial control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
IEE Colloquium on The Application of IEC 61131 to Industrial Control: Improve Your Bottom Line Through High Value Industrial Control Systems (Ref. No. 1999/076)
abstract: IEC1131-3 is a worldwide standard issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and is the first real attempt to standardise programming environments for industrial automation equipment. Initially it was seen as a PLC standard, but is now more widely regarded as applicable to any industrial automation product, including DCSs, motion control and SCADA, to name but a few. The main feature of the standard is that it stipulates a hierarchical structure, a suite of 5 programming languages and standard data types to be used for configuring a process controller. Therefore, once a user is familiar with the standard, not only will they be conversant with a powerful programming environment, but also this environment will be very similar regardless of whose hardware is being used.
